key_insight: Generating possible protein–ligand binding poses is not enough—choosing the right one remains difficult. Pyrite introduces 1,500 pose-pair comparisons, with expert chemists performing near chance despite access to 3D visualization and physics-based scores.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to evaluate systems that rank candidate protein–ligand binding poses, a challenging step in small-molecule drug discovery.
method: Introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark with 1,500 pose pairs spanning diverse protein–ligand complexes.
Frame evaluation as choosing between two candidate binding poses.
Assess expert chemists using 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores to establish a human performance reference.
impact: Pyrite gives AI/ML practitioners a benchmark for evaluating pose-ranking systems beyond candidate generation. Near-chance expert performance highlights the difficulty of the task and the need for more reliable ranking methods.
visual_elements: Side-by-side protein–ligand poses with a 'Which pose is better?' prompt.
Pipeline diagram: candidate pose generation → pairwise ranking → pose selection.
Benchmark card highlighting 1,500 pose pairs across diverse complexes.
Qualitative performance graphic showing expert results near a 50% chance baseline, without inventing an exact score.
paper_title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
paper_authors: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys, Pranav Murugan, Nate Gruver
